# The Size Effect {#sec-size-replication}

{{< include _draft-warning.qmd >}}

[]{#sec-size}

I follow Chapter 9 of @bali2016.
I compare monthly and June-based size, then examine how each relates to subsequent stock returns.
Formation months run from June 1963 through November 2012.

## Calculating Market Capitalization {#reconstruct-the-published-sample}

The book was published in 2016, well before CRSP's CIZ format.
This replication uses the legacy (SIZ) monthly stock and names files, not the CIZ files used in the earlier chapters.
I use a newer legacy snapshot than the authors, with the same sample dates.
See @tbl-data-vintages for the embedded update dates.

Use the share code in force at the end of each month.
Keep share codes 10 and 11, without adding an exchange screen.
The book's measure uses the absolute alternate price and shares outstanding.
CRSP records shares in thousands; dividing their product by 1,000 gives market capitalization in millions of dollars.
Treat zeros as missing.

{{< include _show-code.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| include: false

from eap_pl import build_sizes
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_sizes, "prices", "names", "classified_months")
```

For the annual measure, join each stock to its capitalization at the most recent June.
A stock without a record for that particular June has no annual value.
I do not carry forward an older June observation.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_sizes, "june_caps", "june_year", "stock_months")
```

[]{#compare-four-measures-of-size-and-their-logs}

Convert nominal market capitalization to December 2012 dollars using the [BLS CPI-U, not seasonally adjusted](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCNS).
Use the CPI for the current observation month for both the monthly and the June-based measures, as in the book.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

show_code(build_sizes, "cpi", "cpi_2012", "all_sizes")
```

```{python}
import polars as pl

from eap_pl import build_sizes

first = pl.date(1963, 6, 1)
last = pl.date(2012, 11, 1)
all_sizes = build_sizes()
sizes = all_sizes.filter(
    pl.col("common"), pl.col("month").is_between(first, last),
)
```

The table includes the earlier December market equity needed for book-to-market and December 2012 for the methodologies sample.
It records common-stock eligibility separately so the prior December price remains available when a stock's share code changes.

```{python}
#| include: false

import os

from eap_pl import write_eap_table

assert sizes["month"].n_unique() == 594
assert all_sizes.select(pl.struct("permno", "month").n_unique()).item() == all_sizes.height
assert all_sizes.filter(pl.col("cap").is_not_null())["cap_real"].null_count() == 0
if os.environ.get("EAP_WRITE_SIZES") == "1":
    write_eap_table(all_sizes, "sizes")
```

## Summary Statistics

The mean of the monthly medians describes the middle stock in a typical month.
It is not a median calculated once on the pooled stock-month data.

```{python}
from eap_pl import mean_cross_sections

stats = mean_cross_sections(sizes, {
    "cap": "`cap`", "cap_real": "`cap_real`",
    "log_cap": "`log_cap`", "log_cap_real": "`log_cap_real`",
    "cap_june": "`cap_june`", "cap_june_real": "`cap_june_real`",
    "log_cap_june": "`log_cap_june`", "log_cap_june_real": "`log_cap_june_real`",
})
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-summary
#| tbl-cap: Monthly summary statistics for size (BEM Table 9.1)
#| code-fold: true

stats.eap.show_table()
```

The average monthly mean market capitalization is much larger than the average monthly median, reflecting the concentration of market capitalization in a few stocks.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem9-concentration
#| fig-cap: Share of market capitalization held by the largest stocks (BEM Figure 9.1)
#| code-fold: true

from plotnine_polars import aes

caps = sizes.filter(pl.col("cap").is_not_null()).sort(
    ["month", "cap", "permno"], descending=[False, True, False],
)
fractions = [.01, .05, .10, .25]
shares = (
    caps.with_columns(rank=pl.col("cap").cum_count().over("month"))
    .group_by("month").agg(
        (pl.col("cap").filter(pl.col("rank") <= (p * pl.len()).round()).sum()
         / pl.col("cap").sum()).alias(f"Largest {p:.0%}")
        for p in fractions
    )
    .sort("month")
)
(
    shares.unpivot(index="month", variable_name="group", value_name="share")
    .with_columns(pl.col("group").cast(pl.Enum([f"Largest {p:.0%}" for p in fractions])))
    .ggplot(aes(x="month", y="share", color="group"))
    .geom_line()
    .scale_x_date(date_breaks="10 years", date_labels="%Y")
    .scale_y_continuous(limits=(0, 1), labels=lambda values: [f"{value:.0%}" for value in values])
    .scale_color_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2")
    .labs(x="Month", y="Share of market capitalization", color="")
    .theme_minimal()
    .add_theme(figure_size=(8, 4), legend_position="top")
)
```

## Correlations {#correlation-and-persistence}

Join the size measures to the twelve-month daily beta from @sec-bem-beta.
I take the mean of the monthly cross-sectional correlations.
Below the diagonal are Pearson correlations on winsorized observations, and above it are Spearman correlations on the original ranks.

```{python}
from eap_pl import correlation_matrix, monthly_panel, period_correlations, persistence

panel = monthly_panel(sizes, first, last)
measures = {"cap": "`cap`", "log_cap": "`log_cap`", "cap_june": "`cap_june`",
            "log_cap_june": "`log_cap_june`", "beta": "Beta"}
corr = period_correlations(panel, measures, "month").select(pl.exclude("month").mean())
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-correlations
#| tbl-cap: Cross-sectional correlations for size and beta (BEM Table 9.2)
#| code-fold: true
correlation_matrix(corr.row(0, named=True), measures).eap.show_table()
```

## Persistence

For persistence, match the same stock at a fixed calendar lag, then winsorize both sides within the matched sample at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-persistence
#| tbl-cap: Persistence of nominal size measures (BEM Table 9.3)
#| code-fold: true
size_measures = {k: v for k, v in measures.items() if k != "beta"}
persistence(panel, size_measures, [1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 120]).eap.show_table()
```

## Size and Stock Returns {#size-and-future-returns}

### Univariate Portfolio Analysis

Sort stocks at the end of month $t$ and measure their excess returns in $t+1$, using the delisting rules in @sec-bem-returns.
First use NYSE stocks to calculate the breakpoints, then use all eligible stocks.
In both cases, assign stocks from the full eligible sample.
For the June-based sort, the value weights use June capitalization, as in BEM.
Returns and CAPM alphas are in percent per month.
The $t$-statistics use six Newey–West lags.

```{python}
from eap_pl import bivariate_months, bivariate_panel, fama_macbeth_table, univariate_panel

def size_deciles(nyse):
    return pl.concat([
        univariate_panel(
            panel.with_columns(total=pl.col(cap).sum().over("month")), cap, nyse,
            [
                pl.col(cap).mean().alias("Market cap"),
                pl.col(real).mean().alias("Market cap, 2012 dollars"),
                (100 * pl.col(cap).sum() / pl.col("total").first()).alias("% of market cap"),
                (100 * (pl.col("exchcd") == 1).fill_null(False).mean()).alias("% NYSE"),
                pl.len().alias("Stocks"), pl.col("beta").mean().alias("Beta"),
            ],
            weight=cap,
        ).with_columns(pl.lit(label).alias("Sort"))
        for cap, real, label in [
            ("cap", "cap_real", "Monthly"), ("cap_june", "cap_june_real", "June"),
        ]
    ]).select("Sort", pl.exclude("Sort"))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-deciles
#| tbl-cap: Size deciles using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.4)
#| code-fold: true
size_deciles(nyse=True).eap.show_table()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-deciles
#| tbl-cap: Size deciles using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.5)
#| code-fold: true
size_deciles(nyse=False).eap.show_table()
```

The equal-weighted large-minus-small spread for monthly size is −0.49% per month with NYSE breakpoints and −1.54% with all-stock breakpoints.
The difference comes primarily from the smallest decile.

### Bivariate Portfolio Analysis {#sort-on-beta-and-size}

For a dependent sort, form beta quintiles first and compute size breakpoints within each beta quintile.
For an independent sort, compute beta and size breakpoints separately across the reference universe.
The rows are size quintiles and the columns are beta quintiles.
Average portfolios give each constituent portfolio equal weight each month.

```{python}
def size_quintiles(nyse, dependent):
    monthly = bivariate_months(panel, "beta", "cap", nyse=nyse, dependent=dependent)
    return pl.concat([
        bivariate_panel(monthly, weight, independent=not dependent)
        .with_columns(pl.lit(weight).alias("Weights"))
        for weight in ("EW", "VW")
    ]).select("Weights", pl.exclude("Weights")).rename({"Target": "Size"})
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-dependent
#| tbl-cap: Dependent beta and size sorts using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.6)
#| code-fold: true
size_quintiles(nyse=True, dependent=True).eap.show_table()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-dependent
#| tbl-cap: Dependent beta and size sorts using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.7)
#| code-fold: true
size_quintiles(nyse=False, dependent=True).eap.show_table()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-nyse-independent
#| tbl-cap: Independent beta and size sorts using NYSE breakpoints (BEM Table 9.8)
#| code-fold: true
size_quintiles(nyse=True, dependent=False).eap.show_table()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-all-independent
#| tbl-cap: Independent beta and size sorts using all-stock breakpoints (BEM Table 9.9)
#| code-fold: true
size_quintiles(nyse=False, dependent=False).eap.show_table()
```

### Fama–MacBeth Regression Analysis {#famamacbeth-regressions}

Regress the next month's excess return on log market capitalization, with and without beta.
Winsorize the regressors by month at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles.
Apply six Newey–West lags to the time series of monthly coefficient estimates.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem9-fm
#| tbl-cap: Fama–MacBeth regressions of returns on size (BEM Table 9.10)
#| code-fold: true

specifications = [
    ["log_cap"], ["log_cap", "beta"], ["log_cap_june"], ["log_cap_june", "beta"],
]
fama_macbeth_table(panel, specifications,
                             {"log_cap": "Size", "log_cap_june": "Size FF", "beta": "Beta"}).eap.show_table()
```

## The Size Factor

`smb` is the average of three small-stock portfolios less the average of three big-stock portfolios.
The three portfolios in each size group cover low, middle, and high book-to-market.
Using the same book-to-market groups on both sides reduces the factor's exposure to the value spread.

For the historical factor series I use the monthly Fama–French `smb` from July 1926 through December 2012.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bem9-smb
#| fig-cap: Cumulative returns on the Fama–French `smb` factor (BEM Figure 9.2)
#| code-fold: true
from eap_pl import plot_factor

plot_factor("smb")
```
